item.title: Local Men’s Shed to open new premises with special community event
item.description: A local men's shed will hold a very special open day today to celebrate the launch of its new premises. Killoe Men's Shed meets every Thursday night and offers a range of activities for members. Events will start at 11 o'clock this morning with the opening ceremony set to take place at two o'clock this afternoon. item.title: Motorist arrested on suspicion of drug-driving in Leitrim
item.description: A driver has been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving in Co Leitrim, as part of the gardai’s Christmas road-safety campaign. They also seized a vehicle for having no insurance. A third vehicle was seized because a learner-permit holder wasn’t accompanied by a fully qualified driver. Advertisement

item.title: Carrick-on-Shannon's cinema sold - but not closing down
item.description: Carrick-on-Shannon's cinema has been sold - but it is not closing down. Carrick Cineplex in Cortober has told customers to use gift vouchers by January 4th, 2026 - after which they won't be valid. But it's understood a new operator will be taking over the business after it was sold recently. Advertisement The cinema has had a drop in customers in recent years as streaming services became more popular. Advertisement

item.title: Ireland hit by major fishing quota cut after EU talks
item.description: A local MEP says Ireland’s fishing industry has suffered a major setback following talks at the EU Fisheries Council in Brussels. Ciaran Mullooly says Ireland will lose around 57-thousand tonnes of fishing quota for 2026 - a move he warns will hit coastal communities and put jobs at risk. He says Irish fishermen are being unfairly penalised, despite following strict conservation rules, while non-EU countries continue to overfish. item.title: Rahara residents given relief from flooding this Christmas
item.description: A cabinet minister says the people of Rahara in south Roscommon won't have to endure more flooding 'torture' this Christmas. Lough Funshinagh has caused heartache to many residents over the past decade, as water levels rose sharply. But a temporary pumping solution was activated in March and water levels are controlled this winter. Advertisement Culture Minister Patrick O'Donovan says this is a big relief to residents.

item.title: Revenue seize over €1.27 million in contraband in nationwide operations, including the Midlands
item.description: Revenue officers have seized contraband worth more than €1.27 million in a series of intelligence-led and risk-based operations, including the Midlands. The enforcement actions resulted in significant drug, tobacco, alcohol, and counterfeit goods seizures, along with dozens of weapons. Revenue says the detections reflect its continued focus on tackling smuggling and shadow-economy activity nationwide. item.title: Christmas vigil for Palestine taking place in Roscommon Town this evening
item.description: The Roscommon Palestine Solidarity Campaign is holding a Christmas Vigil for Palestine this afternoon. People are invited to gather beside the crib at The Square in Roscommon Town at 4 o’clock. Organisers say everyone is welcome to come along and show their support. Advertisement

item.title: Water supply disruption warning for parts of County Roscommon
item.description: Uisce Éireann is warning of low water pressure and possible supply outages for customers on the North East Regional Water Scheme in County Roscommon. The issue follows problems at the Grange Water Treatment Plant, affecting areas including Strokestown, Ballyleague, Ballybeg, Elphin, Tarmonbarry, Slatta and Scramogue. item.title: St Dominic's fall in All-Ireland camogie bid
item.description: St. Dominic’s All-Ireland camogie hopes fell at the last hurdle as Brídíní Óga Glenravel claimed a five-point victory. Torie Edgar’s accuracy procured a second AIB All-Ireland junior club camogie title for Brídíní Óga Glenravel in three years. The Brídíní Óga captain hit 0-7, including six frees, to guide her side to victory. As St Dominic’s were left to rue eight second-half wides.
